extracted.intended_audience: political reformers, legislators, students of political theory, and advocates of electoral reform
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and normative principles for structuring representative government and electoral systems so as to avoid class domination, ensure proportional representation of minorities, preserve local interests, and raise the intellectual quality of representatives. Focuses especially on mechanisms (e.g., Hare/STV, limited votes, cumulative voting) that achieve these ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corruption by power
rubrics_metrics.description: Power tends to call forth and foster selfish and short-sighted dispositions; men and classes are corrupted by the possession of power and become worshippers of themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design government institutions recognizing that possession of power increases self-regarding motives and weakens regard for distant consequences; do not assume benevolent behavior from those in power. Antipattern: assuming private-station behavior predicts conduct when that agent holds power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for human nature as it is
rubrics_metrics.description: Governments must be made for human beings as they are, or as they are capable of speedily becoming; it is unrealistic to require that average citizens act from exalted disinterested principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional design should not presuppose that the majority will act from disinterested public spirit or posterity-regard; instead, provide structures that check obvious, immediate self-interest. Avoid constitutions that require citizens routinely to act contrary to their visible and immediate interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against class legislation / sinister interests
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the greatest dangers of democracy (and all governments) is class legislation: measures intended for the immediate benefit of the dominant class to the lasting detriment of the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A principal goal in constitutional design is to provide efficacious securities to prevent any class or coalition from using government to pursue sectional advantage. Consider checks that limit ability of any single class to exercise preponderant influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance competing class interests in representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The representative system should be organized so that the chief socio-economic divisions (roughly 'laborers' and 'employers' and their affinities) are balanced, each influencing about an equal number of votes in the legislature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for institutional arrangements where opposing class interests can check one another and where minorities combining with persons of higher motives can prevent sectional injustice. Antipattern: systems that concentrate representation in the hands of one class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportional representation of minorities
rubrics_metrics.description: A real democracy requires that minorities be adequately represented proportionately—man for man they should be as fully represented as the majority; a system that wipes out minorities is not true democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure electoral mechanics allow minorities (including dispersed minorities) to return representatives in proportion to their numbers. Antipattern: winner-take-all local majorities that leave sizable minorities with no representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of equal suffrage — equal individual weight
rubrics_metrics.description: Equal democracy means every individual counts equally; current practice often gives the majority only a majority-of-the-majority, not the majority of all individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electoral rules should be assessed by whether each individual's vote has equal effective weight in the summing-up. Antipattern: institutional arrangements that produce parliamentary majorities not reflecting a majority of individual electors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable cross-constituency aggregation of minority votes
rubrics_metrics.description: Real equality of representation requires that any set of electors, amounting to the average constituency number wherever they reside, be able to combine to return a representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design voting rules so that like-minded minorities scattered across constituencies can aggregate their votes to elect a candidate (rather than being permanently wasted in each local contest). This combats concentration of representation by local majorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited-vote and cumulative-vote methods as partial remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals such as multi-member constituencies with each elector allowed fewer votes, or allowing an elector to give all votes to one candidate, can enable local minorities (e.g., one-third) to return a member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These schemes are improvements over simple plurality but are imperfect: they fail to represent minorities smaller than the threshold and do not allow widely-dispersed minorities to combine across districts. Treat them as makeshifts toward fuller proportionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hare's personal representation (single transferable vote) scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Unit of representation determined by quota (voters divided by seats); electors may vote for any candidate anywhere and list preferences; votes counted centrally; a candidate that reaches the quota is returned; surplus votes are redistributed to next preferences until houses are filled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This scheme enables proportionate representation of all sufficiently numerous minorities, preserves local representation where a locality exceeds a quota, allows electors to support national figures, and reduces wasted votes. Practical elements: quota calculation by averages, central counting, handling surpluses and transferred votes by prescribed methods, and use of lot as a fallback. The text endorses Hare's plan as feasible and near-ideal for the objectives described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow voters to rank preferences to avoid wasting votes
rubrics_metrics.description: An elector may deliver a voting paper containing other names in addition to his first preference; if his first choice fails to reach the quota, the vote counts for his next chosen candidate, and so on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferential ranking prevents votes for unsuccessful local candidates from being lost; it increases the effective representation options for voters and helps minorities obtain representation without abandoning their primary preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quota limit and surplus redistribution rules
rubrics_metrics.description: No more votes than the quota should be counted for any candidate's return; any surplus of votes beyond the quota should be reallocated to other candidates on voters' lists, and methods must determine which of a candidate's ballots are used for his return.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt clear rules for selecting which ballots count toward a candidate's quota and for transferring the surplus (proportional transfer, specified selection rules, or lot if necessary). Proper surplus allocation prevents extremely popular candidates from absorbing nearly all suffrages and enables full representation of others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public transparency and verifiability of count
rubrics_metrics.description: Voting papers and all elements of the calculation should be placed in public repositories accessible to concerned parties; if any one entitled to be returned is not, he should be able to prove it easily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure open records of ballots and count procedures so candidates and voters can verify results and detect errors or malfeasance. Transparency supports trust in complex counting systems like Hare's.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve local representation while expanding choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Though national proportional mechanisms are used, valuable aspects of local representation (members commissioned to look after locality interests) should be preserved; where a locality has many more voters than the quota, the majority will usually prefer a local representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design systems to retain local seats for local matters while enabling minorities to seek representation elsewhere. Antipattern: abandoning local accountability entirely in favor of only national lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raise intellectual and moral calibre of representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Systemic rules should make it possible for able men of national reputation (without local influence or party machines) to be returned, thereby improving the intellectual quality of the assembly and countering collective mediocrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanisms that allow votes for national figures (and aggregation of minority support) incentivize skilled, independent candidates to stand and increase competition for qualified representatives. Antipattern: electoral rules that limit opportunities to local influence, lavish expenditure, or party patronage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce party-machine selection of lowest-common-denominator candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: Current party practices force majorities to accept nominees who are palatable to the weakest or most narrow-minded portions of the party, producing poor-quality candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electoral designs that allow voters to look beyond local party slates and support nationally-known or better-quality candidates will compel parties to present stronger nominees or risk losing votes to other candidates.
